drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start in an athletic position with knees slightly bent. Stride and pause — make sure you feel balanced before swinging. Keep your eyes on the ball all the way through contact. Drive through the ball, don't just hit it.

drills.description: A one-handed hitting drill from Ripken Baseball that isolates each hand individually. Players hit off a tee using only their bottom hand, then only their top hand, to build strength, bat control, and proper swing path in each hand independently.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Use a lighter bat for this drill. Bottom hand only: focus on pulling the knob of the bat toward the ball. Top hand only: focus on driving through the ball with your palm pushing forward. Keep your body rotation — don't just arm-swing.

drills.drill_name: 10 Best Baseball Hitting Drills for Kids
drills.description: A compilation of 10 kid-friendly hitting drills from MOJO Sports including tee work, soft toss variations, and fun competitive drills that keep young players engaged while building proper swing mechanics and confidence at the plate.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Keep your eyes on the ball the whole time. Grip the bat with your knocking knuckles lined up. Take a small step toward the pitcher when you swing. Swing level through the ball — try to hit line drives.

drills.drill_name: How to Hit a Baseball Step by Step
drills.description: A step-by-step instructional video from Ultimate Baseball Training breaking down how to hit a baseball from the ground up. Covers proper grip, balanced stance, loading the hands, controlled stride, swing path through the zone, and complete follow-through.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Line up your knocking knuckles on the bat. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent. Load your hands back near your ear as you stride forward. Swing down through the ball and finish high over your opposite shoulder.

drills.drill_name: Must-Do Youth Pitching Drills for Beginners
drills.description: A comprehensive collection of must-do pitching drills specifically for young and beginning pitchers. Breaks down the pitching motion into simple, manageable parts including Balance Point Drill, Knee Drill, and Stride Drill that youth players can understand and execute.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Lift your knee to your belt buckle and hold for 2 seconds before striding. Point your glove at the target. Land softly on your front foot. Finish with your chest over your front knee.

drills.description: MOJO Sports covers 9 top pitching drills for kids including the Kneel of Fortune (upper body rotation), Balance Beam (steady delivery using cones), Flamingo (single-leg strength/control), and Towel Slap (mechanics without a ball). Drills break down pitching into fun, manageable parts.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stand like a flamingo — strong and balanced on one leg. Snap the towel at the target like you're throwing the ball. Keep your eyes on the target the whole time. Stride toward home plate, not to the side.

drills.description: Former pro pitcher Dan Blewett demonstrates the Rocker Drill — his top recommended pitching drill for youth players. The drill teaches proper hip-led weight shift and front-side drive, creating uphill shoulders that improve velocity and command.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Rock back, then drive your front hip toward the catcher. Keep your shoulders tilted uphill as you stride. Pull your glove to your chest — don't let it drop. Feel your weight stay back as your hips lead the way.

drills.description: A game-speed blocking drill with unpredictable balls in the dirt — the catcher must read and react rather than pre-set. For catchers who already own solid blocking mechanics.
common_flaws_fixed: balls in the dirt get past
bails on balls in the dirt
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Mix locations randomly and don't telegraph. Score each rep: blocked-in-front = 2, blocked-away = 1, past = 0; track weekly. Add a runner-on-third scenario so recovery-to-throw matters.
success_markers: 8+ of 10 random balls kept in front
Recovers to throwing position within one second
No flinch or head-turn at game velocity
drills.safety_notes: Full catcher's gear required. Game-speed dirt balls only for catchers with established blocking form.

drills.description: Catcher footwork patterns for throwing to second at game speed — replace, jab-step, and transfer mechanics that shorten pop time and control the running game.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Time every rep glove-to-glove. Cue 'feet start the throw' — the exchange happens while the feet replace. Start dry (no ball), then from a partner's toss, then live machine pitches.
success_markers: Pop time trends down week over week
Transfer happens during footwork, not after
Throws arrive on the bag-side of second consistently
drills.safety_notes: Arm-care warm-up before throw-downs; cap volume at ~20 full-intensity throws per session for youth arms.

drills.drill_name: Bent-Leg Slide Basics — The Right Way to Slide
drills.description: Intro to correct bent-leg sliding: when to start the slide, tucking one leg into the figure-4, keeping hands up, and avoiding the habits that cause injuries.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Teach on grass in socks or on a sliding mat first — never on dirt day one. Cue 'sit into it, hands to the sky.' Start from a walk, then jog, then run. Mark a start line about two body lengths from the base.
drills.reps_guidance: 10-15 slides per session, building speed gradually
success_markers: Slides on the seat/hip, not the knees
Hands stay up through the slide
Starts the slide at the marked distance without hesitation
drills.safety_notes: No headfirst slides for beginners. Slide on grass, wet grass, or a mat before ever sliding on dirt; remove cleats for first sessions.

drills.description: Station-based sliding reps for teams: high-repetition bent-leg slides in a controlled setting to build comfort and consistency once players know the basic form.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run as a rotating station during practice. Every player gets volume without dirt burn. Watch for the trail leg flattening out — keep the figure-4. Add a coach pointing left/right so runners slide to a side of the bag.
success_markers: Same slide shape every rep
Can slide to either side of the bag on command
No slowing down before the slide starts
drills.safety_notes: Use mats or grass for volume work; check the sliding lane is clear of equipment between reps.

drills.description: Game-speed pop-up slide: sliding into the bag on the bent leg and using momentum to pop up ready to advance on an overthrow.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Only after the basic bent-leg slide is automatic. Cue 'slide through the bag, not to it' — momentum carries the runner up onto the planted foot. Pair with a coach throwing simulated overthrows to train the advance read.
drills.reps_guidance: 8-10 pop-up slides, last 4 with an overthrow read
success_markers: Pops to standing without using hands
Eyes find the ball immediately after the slide
Advances confidently on overthrows in scrimmages
drills.safety_notes: Full-speed pop-up slides on dirt only after mat/grass mastery; no headfirst variations.

drills.drill_name: 10 Best Baseball Throwing Drills for Kids
drills.description: MOJO Sports presents 10 structured throwing drills for youth players including Extreme Catch, Selfies, Over Under, Clean Up Crew, and Bullseye — each designed as a game-like activity that teaches proper throwing fundamentals while keeping kids engaged and competitive.
common_flaws_fixed: slow transitions from catch to throw
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Use a 4-seam grip every time. Step toward your target. Follow through so your throwing hand ends by your opposite knee. Compete with yourself — try to hit the target more times each round.
success_markers: Hits a partner's chest on most throws from 30+ feet.

drills.drill_name: Steal Breaks — Reading the Pitcher & First Move
drills.description: Teaches the steal break: what runners watch on the pitcher, when to take off, and the explosive crossover first move. Coach-facing so it translates straight to team practice.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Line the whole team up off an imaginary first base facing a coach simulating a pitcher. On first move: break. Cue 'sink, cross over, run through second's back corner.' Call out what tipped the pitcher's move each rep.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 6 breaks (react to leg lift, first move, pickoff mix)
success_markers: Breaks on first move, not on a guess
Crossover step gains ground toward second
Freezes correctly on pickoff moves

drills.description: The secondary lead and the delayed steal: timing shuffles with the pitch, reading the catcher, and stealing bases without elite speed.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Rep the two-shuffle secondary timed to the pitch crossing the zone. For the delayed steal, break as the catcher's throw goes back to the pitcher. Works especially well at levels where catchers lob returns.
success_markers: Secondary lead lands as the pitch crosses the plate
Momentum moving toward the next base at contact
Successfully times a delayed steal in scrimmage

drills.description: Coach Justin demonstrates essential footwork drills for youth catchers covering proper receiving stance, secondary stance with runners on, quick transfer mechanics from catching to throwing position, and pop-up footwork for throwing to second base.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Feet shoulder-width apart, weight on the balls of your feet. When runners are on, move to your secondary stance — slightly more upright, ready to throw. Right foot replaces left foot when throwing to 2nd. Quick feet equal quick throws.

drills.drill_name: Simple Base Running Drills for Youth Practice
drills.description: Coaches Duke and Steve from Dominate the Diamond demonstrate a game-like baserunning setup using three angled cones to simulate multiple first bases, allowing three groups to work simultaneously on steal breaks, lead-offs, and base-running mechanics while maximizing reps.
common_flaws_fixed: running past bases without proper turns
equipment_needed: Full baseball field or open area
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Set up 3 cones on an angle so every runner can SEE the pitcher. Eyes on the pitcher the whole time. When you break, turn your hips FIRST, keep feet low, push off hard with your back foot. Stay athletic and ready to move.

drills.description: Coach Justin presents a 5-point checklist every baserunner should execute every time they reach base. Systematically walks through proper baserunning habits including taking a lead, knowing the situation, reading the ball, understanding when to tag up, and when to be aggressive.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Every time you get on base: (1) Find your base coach and listen, (2) Take your lead, (3) Know how many outs, (4) Know where the ball is at ALL times, (5) Be ready to GO on every pitch. Practice until it's automatic.

drills.description: Coach Bougie demonstrates 5 progressive blocking drills: Pre-Set Blocks, Side-to-Side Slides, Twist and Block, Inch Worms, and Rapid Fire. Each drill builds on the previous, creating a full blocking progression from basic to game-speed.
equipment_needed: Catcher's gear (chest protector, shin guards, helmet, mitt)
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hips BACK, hands DOWN — make a home plate shape with your arms. Exhale just before the ball hits your body to soften like a pillow. Chin down — try to watch the ball hit your chest protector. Start with tennis balls if you're nervous.
success_markers: Drops to the knees with chest over the ball, hips back and hands down, and keeps blocked balls in front.

drills.drill_name: How to Run the Bases — Pro Tips
drills.description: YouGoProBaseball demonstrates proper base-running technique including running through first base on ground balls, rounding bases efficiently by hitting the inside corner with the right foot, making banana turns for extra bases, and fundamentals of running form on the basepaths.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: On a ground ball — RUN HARD through first base. Don't slow down! On an outfield hit — start curving early (banana path), hit the INSIDE corner with your right foot, and look for the ball. Touch EVERY base.

drills.drill_name: Baseball Arm Stretches and Pre-Throwing Warm-Up
drills.description: Coach Justin demonstrates essential arm stretches and a complete throwing warm-up routine covering dynamic stretches and arm care movements that should be performed before every throwing session to prepare the arm and prevent injury.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Always warm up your arm before throwing — never throw cold. Do arm circles forward and backward. Stretch gently — don't force it. Make these stretches part of your routine every single practice and game day.

drills.drill_name: Complete Pitching and Throwing Warm-Up Routine
drills.description: A complete pre-throwing warm-up and arm care routine designed for all ages. Covers dynamic movements, shoulder activation exercises, and a progressive throwing warm-up sequence that prepares the arm for practice or games.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Do this routine before every practice and game. Start with big arm circles, then get smaller. Warm up your whole body, not just your arm. If your arm feels tired or sore, tell your coach right away.

drills.drill_name: 8 Baseball Warm-Up Exercises You Must Do
drills.description: A comprehensive 8-exercise dynamic warmup routine covering high knees, butt kicks, leg swings, arm circles, torso rotations, shuffle steps, backpedals, and progressive throwing. Designed as a complete pre-game and pre-practice warmup sequence.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Do each exercise for 15-20 yards. Keep your chest up and core tight. Don't rush — quality movement beats speed. Finish with easy throws before going full speed. Never skip your warm-up!

drills.description: A dynamic warmup routine specifically targeting arm stretches and shoulder mobility for baseball players. Focuses on preparing the upper body for throwing, batting, and fielding through active stretching movements.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Move your arms through the full range of motion slowly. Never force a stretch — go to where you feel a gentle pull. Do this BEFORE you pick up a ball. Warm up to throw, don't throw to warm up!

drills.description: ZONEDSportsAcademy (the training facility arm of Dominate the Diamond) presents a base running circuit combining sprint mechanics, agility, and coordination into a baseball-specific athletic development circuit that develops speed, explosiveness, and body control.
common_flaws_fixed: poor body control when changing direction
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run hard around the bases using good form — pump your arms and lean into your turns. Hit the inside of each base. Try to beat your time each round. Stay low through the turns — don't pop up tall.

drills.drill_name: Baseball Dynamic Stretches for Youth Players
drills.description: A physical therapy-designed dynamic stretching routine tailored for baseball players. Focuses on baseball-specific movement patterns to increase flexibility, improve body awareness, and reduce injury risk through controlled, active stretches.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: These stretches should feel like a gentle pull, never pain. Move smoothly and control each stretch. Great for injury prevention — do it every single practice and game day. If anything hurts, stop and tell your coach.

drills.description: Hit with one hand to build strength and feel.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Top hand: palm up through contact. Bottom hand: knob to ball.

drills.drill_name: Pro Base-Stealing Package — Leads, Reads & Jumps
drills.description: Game-speed stealing package: primary lead distance, reading pitcher tells and pickoff moves, and maximizing the jump against live pitching.
equipment_needed: live pitcher or coach on mound
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run against a live pitcher working from the stretch. Chart every rep: safe jump / late / picked. Teach one tell at a time (heel lift, shoulder lean, head pattern). Time first-move-to-second and track improvement.
success_markers: Identifies the pitcher's tell and states it out loud
Jump rate improves on the weekly chart
Returns standing on pickoffs — never dives late from an overextended lead

drills.drill_name: Calm Rundowns — Push Back, Follow Your Throw
drills.description: Takes the panic out of youth rundowns: pushing the runner back toward the previous base, following your throw, and getting the out in as few throws as possible.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Layer in the rule: always push the runner back toward the base he came from, and always follow your throw to the end of the opposite line. Add a second runner variant once the basic rotation is automatic.
success_markers: Runner is always moving back toward the trailing base
Thrower follows his throw every time without reminding
Backup fielder is in line before the throw is made
drills.safety_notes: Helmets on runners; keep rundown lanes clear of bats and loose balls.

drills.description: Players hold a PVC pipe across their shoulders and practice rotating around their axis without swinging a bat. The pipe gives visual feedback if the player is swaying, dipping, or losing posture during rotation rather than rotating in place.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Put the PVC pipe across your shoulders like a yoke. Now rotate — the ends of the pipe should stay level the whole time. If one end drops, you're losing your axis. Think of a spinning top — it spins in place, it doesn't move around. That's what your swing should feel like.

drills.description: A simplified cut-and-relay system built for Little League fields: where each fielder goes on balls to each outfield spot, kept simple enough for young teams to run in games.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Walk the whole team through each scenario at half speed with no ball first — every player physically moves to their spot. Then add a rolled ball, then a thrown ball. Quiz players: 'ball in the right-center gap, runner on first — where do you go?'
drills.reps_guidance: Walk-through of 4 scenarios, then 2 live reps each
success_markers: Every player moves somewhere on contact — nobody stands still
Cutoff man is in line between outfielder and target base
Team can name their assignment for each gap without prompting
drills.safety_notes: Sequence throws so only one ball is live at a time; young fielders should never turn their back on an incoming throw.

drills.description: A partner kneels to the side and tosses balls underhand into the hitter's strike zone. The hitter tracks the ball from the tosser's hand through contact, focusing on driving the ball up the middle and maintaining a balanced finish.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Watch the ball leave my hand. Let the ball get into your hitting zone — don't chase it too early. Stay balanced and drive through the ball toward the middle of the field. Finish with your hands high.

drills.description: Underhand tosses from in front to simulate pitches.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Track the ball. Stay back. Hit through the middle.

drills.description: Hitters use only their bottom hand to swing at a ball on the tee. This drill isolates the lead arm and trains the knob to ball path — the direct, short path the hands should take toward the baseball.
equipment_needed: one-hand training bat or short bat
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hold the bat with just your bottom hand. Think knob to ball — pull the knob of the bat directly toward the ball as fast as you can. This one is harder because it's usually your weaker hand. Keep your elbow close to your body as you start the swing.

drills.drill_name: High Tee Drill — Hitting Up in the Zone
drills.description: Coach Duke Baxter sets up the tee at the top of the strike zone and trains hitters to take a short, compact path to high pitches. Players focus on backspin line drives toward second base rather than trying to swing down on the ball.
common_flaws_fixed: slow bat speed on high pitches
equipment_needed: Adjustable batting tee (set to high position)
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Set the tee up near your chest. The high pitch wants a SHORT, QUICK move — not a big loopy swing. Drive through the ball and try to hit a backspin line drive toward second base. If you feel your barrel dragging behind your hands, speed up your hands!

drills.description: The Albert Pujols drill — hitters drop to one knee in their launch position and work purely on upper-body rotation and hand path to the ball. Eliminates lower body mechanics so players can isolate and feel proper hand/shoulder action.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Get down on your back knee. From this position it's all about your hands and rotation. Drive your top hand through the ball — aim for backspin line drives to the opposite field gap. Feel your shoulders rotating, not just your arms.

drills.description: Coach Duke Baxter of Dominate the Diamond / Zoned Sports Academy runs a full coach's clinic covering all hitting fundamentals in a sequential, easy-to-teach format. Designed for coaches teaching players the complete mechanics of a fundamentally sound swing.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Let's build your swing one piece at a time: (1) Grip, (2) Stance, (3) Load back, (4) Stride soft, (5) Swing, (6) Finish. Master one before moving to the next. Every good hitter does all six things every single swing.

drills.drill_name: 5 Essential Hitting Drills for Youth Baseball
drills.description: Former MLB player Jermaine Curtis covers 5 essential hitting drills tailored specifically for youth players. He uses MLB-level swing analysis to explain WHY each drill works, then demonstrates each in a simple, youth-accessible format.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Great hitters make it look easy because they practice the basics perfectly. Do each drill slowly first, then build up speed. Your hips start the swing — your hands follow. Practice until the right feeling becomes automatic.

drills.drill_name: 10 Best Baseball Hitting Drills for Kids
drills.description: MOJO Sports presents 10 kid-friendly hitting drills including tee work, soft toss variations, and fun competitive formats with unique names that keep young players engaged while building real swing mechanics and plate confidence.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: These drills are supposed to be fun! The more you enjoy practicing, the better you'll get. Work hard on each one, but make it a game — try to beat your last score or challenge a teammate. Good mechanics AND fun go together.

drills.description: Tee set high to practice high-pitch swings.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Short, quick path. Drive through with backspin.

drills.drill_name: Line Relay Race — Catch, Turn, Throw
drills.description: A repeatable line-relay drill: lining up to the ball, presenting a big target with hands up, and making quick catch-turn-throw transfers down the line. Run it as a race between two lines.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Two lines of 4-5 players, 60-90 feet apart per link. Cue 'big hands, catch, turn glove-side, throw through the chest.' First line to run the ball down and back wins. Shrink spacing for younger kids.
success_markers: Relay man's hands are up calling for the ball before it arrives
Turns glove-side automatically
Ball travels line-to-line without hitting the ground
drills.safety_notes: Match throwing distances to arm strength — shorten the links for 8-10U rather than letting kids max-effort long throws.

drills.drill_name: Hitting Tips for Tee Ball (4-5 Year Olds)
drills.description: A parent-friendly video teaching the absolute fundamentals of hitting to very young players just starting tee ball. Focuses on fun, confidence building, and the most basic mechanics — grip and watching the ball — without overwhelming young beginners.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hold the bat like you're shaking hands with it. Look at the ball on the tee and don't take your eyes off it. Swing like you're trying to swat a big fly — whoosh! High five when you make contact! Every swing is a great swing when you're learning.

drills.drill_name: Catch and Crush Drill — Stay Closed
drills.description: A drill where the hitter catches the baseball with their top hand and holds it briefly over the tee before initiating the swing. This teaches the hitter to keep the upper body closed while the lower body initiates — creating the separation and torque that generates power.
common_flaws_fixed: no separation between upper and lower body
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Catch the ball and HOLD it over the tee. Let your hips start to open... but keep your shoulders closed. Feel the tension in your core? That's torque — THAT'S power! Now crush through the ball. The longer you stay closed, the more power you generate.

drills.drill_name: Shoulder Swings — Stay Short to the Ball
drills.description: Without a ball, players swing keeping their back elbow tucked into their hip slot as they initiate the swing. The drill creates the sensation of a short, quick path to the hitting zone and eliminates the long, loop cast most youth hitters develop.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start in your stance. Begin your swing — but keep your back elbow tucked tight to your side. Don't let it fly out. This is what staying short feels like. Do 20 slow motion swings focusing only on that back elbow staying close. Then add speed.

drills.description: Players throw a frisbee from a baseball stance using their swing motion. The frisbee provides natural feedback on hip opening timing and finish direction — if hips open too early, the frisbee sails the wrong way; if the finish is correct, it flies straight to the target.
common_flaws_fixed: not finishing swing in direction of target
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hold the frisbee in your bottom hand and throw it from your batting stance. Your hips open — and the frisbee follows. Try to send the frisbee toward center field. Did it go there? Good hip rotation! Did it sail to the side? Your hips opened too early or too late.

drills.description: Popularized by Hall of Famer Barry Larkin, players step into the swing with a walking approach — building momentum before making contact. The walk-through teaches how to transfer linear momentum into rotational power, dramatically increasing bat speed at contact.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Take a small walking step before you swing — like you're walking through the ball. Build momentum as you step into it and DRIVE through contact. Feel how much more power you have? Now you know what a real weight transfer feels like. Use that feeling in your normal swing.

drills.drill_name: Bucket Drill — Stay in Your Legs
drills.description: Players sit on a bucket in their athletic batting crouch, then stand up into their load and take a swing while trying to maintain the same bent-knee posture they had sitting down. The bucket gives a tactile reminder of proper leg bend and posture.
common_flaws_fixed: popping up out of stance during swing
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start sitting on the bucket in your batting crouch. Now stand up into your swing — but try to KEEP the same knee bend you had while sitting. Don't pop tall! Stay low through your swing the same way you were sitting. That low position is where your power comes from.

drills.drill_name: Two-Tee Drill — Contact at Different Heights
drills.description: Two tees are set up at different heights — one chest high, one knee high. The hitter swings at the lower tee while the upper tee acts as a ceiling, teaching the batter to adjust bat path and maintain extension across different pitch locations.
common_flaws_fixed: poor adjustment to different pitch levels
equipment_needed: Two batting tees set at different heights
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Swing at the LOWER tee without hitting the upper one. That means your bat path has to stay on the right level — not too high, not too low. If you hit the top tee, your bat went above the ball. Adjust and try again. This teaches you to hit any pitch in the zone.

drills.description: Team cutoff and relay responsibilities by situation — who the cutoff man is on balls to each outfield spot, and how infielders and outfielders communicate to hit the cutoff.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Add runners so decisions are real: runner on first, ball to left-center — where's the throw? Let the cutoff man call 'cut two / cut three / let it go' loudly. Rotate players through cutoff roles so everyone learns both ends.
success_markers: Outfield throws come down through the cutoff man's head height
Cutoff man makes a loud call on every ball
Correct base chosen on 4 of 5 situational reps
drills.safety_notes: One live ball at a time; runners wear helmets during live cutoff reps.

drills.description: A feeder bounces balls off the ground at an angle into the hitting zone, creating an unpredictable ball path similar to a changeup or pitch with late movement. Forces hitters to track, adjust, and stay patient through varied ball movement.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stay patient — let the ball bounce and come back up into the zone. Don't panic when the ball does something unexpected. Track it all the way into the hitting zone. Your job is to stay balanced, read the ball, and adjust your swing. Stay relaxed!

drills.description: Named after Adam Sandler's movie character, players take a walking step behind them before launching into their swing. This exaggerated drill teaches how lower body momentum dramatically amplifies bat speed and power, giving young players a visceral feel for hip-driven force.
mechanic_focus: creating bat speed through body movement
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Step back with your back foot, then drive forward and swing — like Happy Gilmore! Feel how much FASTER your bat moves with all that momentum? That hip drive is real power. You won't swing like this in a game, but now you know what using your whole body feels like. Use THAT feeling.

drills.description: Players practice making adjustments with two strikes — choking up on the bat, widening their stance slightly, shortening their stride, and prioritizing making contact over power. Coach emphasizes different mental approach with two strikes versus 0-0 count.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: With two strikes, choke up 1-2 inches on the bat. Widen your stance a little. Make a shorter stride. Your job now is to PUT THE BALL IN PLAY — no strikeouts! Protect the plate and go to the opposite field if you have to. A two-strike hit is one of the best feelings in baseball.

drills.drill_name: The Track and Catch Drill — Head on the Ball
drills.description: Players take their normal swing but at the moment of contact they freeze and catch the ball with their free hand. This forces them to keep their head completely still and eyes locked on the ball all the way through the contact zone — fixing the most common youth hitting problem.
mechanic_focus: keeping head on ball through contact
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Swing — and try to CATCH the ball at the contact point! You can't catch what you can't see. That means you have to keep your eyes on the ball ALL the way through your swing. If you miss the catch, your head moved. Freeze at contact and look at where the ball is.

drills.drill_name: Machine-Fed Relay Sequences at Game Speed
drills.description: Game-speed cutoff and relay team sequences modeled on Vanderbilt's practice, using machine-fed balls to rep full outfield-to-infield relays at high tempo.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Machine or fungo fires balls into the gaps on a fixed interval so tempo never drops. Run double-cut sequences on balls to the wall. Score runs-prevented vs. bases-gained to make it competitive between defensive groups.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 5 relay sequences at full speed
success_markers: Relay throws are caught chest-high moving toward the target
Double cut executes with the trail man communicating
Sequence time from outfield touch to tag drops week over week
drills.safety_notes: Full-intensity relay throws count toward daily throwing volume — run this early in practice on fresh arms.

drills.description: Work on proper batting stance fundamentals.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Athletic position. Knees bent. Weight balanced.

drills.drill_name: Youth Pitching Mechanics — Complete Step-by-Step Breakdown
drills.description: Former professional pitcher Dan Blewett walks through the complete pitching motion step-by-step, explaining every phase in simple language a youth player can understand. Covers grip, balance point, hip lead, arm action, and finish — the definitive beginner pitching mechanics reference.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Let's build your delivery one piece at a time: (1) Grip the ball across the seams, (2) Get balanced on your back leg, (3) Lead with your hip toward home plate, (4) Keep your elbow at shoulder height, (5) Finish by throwing your arm down across your body. Master each step before moving on.

drills.drill_name: The Rocker Drill — Hip Lead & Weight Shift
drills.description: Dan Blewett's signature drill used throughout his professional career. Pitchers rock their weight back then drive their front hip toward home plate before the arm begins. Trains the hip lead action that keeps weight back and creates uphill shoulders — the most important mechanical fix for youth pitchers who lose velocity and command.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Rock back on your back foot... now drive your HIP toward home plate — not your shoulder! Your hip goes first, your arm follows. Feel like your shoulders are tilting uphill as you stride. If your shoulder gets to home plate before your hip does, you've leaked your energy and lost command.

drills.drill_name: The Heel-Toe Drill — Front Foot Landing
drills.description: A simple drill from Dan Blewett where pitchers focus on landing with their front foot heel first — slightly closed (toed inward). This position keeps the hips loaded and prevents the common fault of landing with the foot turned out, which bleeds power and reduces command.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: When your front foot lands, try to land on your heel and keep your toes pointing slightly toward third base (for righties). Don't let your foot turn open toward home plate. If your front foot is open when you land, your hip rotation disappears. Heel down, toes slightly in — then rotate through it.

drills.drill_name: The Lawnmower Drill — Arm Action & Wrist Snap
drills.description: Named for the pulling motion of starting a lawnmower, this Dan Blewett drill isolates the arm action and wrist snap phase of the delivery. Pitchers pull their arm down and through — mimicking the lawnmower pull — building a loose, whip-like arm action and proper wrist snap without throwing a ball.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Pull your arm like you're starting a lawnmower — fast and loose! Your arm should feel like a wet noodle, not a stiff board. Snap your wrist at the bottom of the pull. The faster and looser your arm feels, the better. Tight arms lose velocity — stay relaxed!

drills.description: Use chalk line to check stride direction.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Land your front foot just to the left of the line (for righties).

drills.description: A simple pickle setup — two bases, two fielders, one runner — teaching kids to run hard at the runner, hold the ball up, and make one crisp throw for the tag.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue 'run him back, ball up by your ear, one throw.' The receiving fielder calls 'now!' for the throw. Rotate every player through both fielder spots and runner. Count throws out loud — celebrate one-throw outs.
success_markers: Fielder sprints at the runner instead of hesitating
Ball stays visible above the shoulder — no pump fakes
Most outs recorded in two throws or fewer
drills.safety_notes: Runners wear helmets; tags applied with the glove, no arm swings at head height.

drills.description: Players stand on one leg like a flamingo for increasing time periods — 5 seconds, 10 seconds, 30 seconds. This simple pre-pitching balance drill builds the single-leg stability every pitcher needs to maintain balance throughout their delivery without any baseball equipment required.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stand on one foot like a flamingo — arms out to the side. How long can you hold it without putting your other foot down? Try to work up to 30 seconds. Close your eyes for an extra challenge! Strong balance = strong pitching. Practice this every day, even at home while watching TV.

drills.drill_name: Towel Drill — Arm Speed & Release Point
drills.description: The pitcher holds a folded dish towel instead of a ball and goes through their complete delivery. A partner or cone is placed at the expected release point distance, and the pitcher snaps the towel to tag it. No arm strain, full mechanics — teaches proper extension and a consistent forward release point without putting stress on the arm.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hold the towel and throw your complete delivery — try to snap the towel on the target out in front! If you can't reach the target, your release point is too far back. If you overshoot it, you're releasing too late. Snap it right at the target. This drill is great to do every day — no arm fatigue, full mechanics practice!

drills.drill_name: Kneel-Down (Wrist Snap) Drill — Release Point & Backspin
drills.description: Both pitcher and partner kneel on the ground, 15-20 feet apart. From this position, players throw using only their forearm and wrist snap — no lower body, no shoulder rotation. Isolates the final critical phase of ball release and teaches proper backspin and wrist mechanics from close range.
common_flaws_fixed: throwing with entire arm not forearm/wrist
drills.ai_coaching_notes: From your knees, throw only using your forearm and wrist — everything below your elbow. Snap your wrist through the ball and try to put backspin on it. The ball should spin straight back at you like a wheel — not sideways. Feel your fingers pull down the back of the ball as you release. That's what creates a good fastball.

drills.drill_name: Square Hips / Hip Lock Drill — Hip-Shoulder Separation
drills.description: Pitchers work on squaring their hips to the plate at front foot landing while keeping their throwing shoulder back. The drill teaches the critical separation between hip rotation (early) and shoulder rotation (later) that creates torque and velocity. The harder the hip locks, the harder the shoulder and arm whip through.
common_flaws_fixed: hips and shoulders rotating together (no separation)
drills.ai_coaching_notes: When your front foot hits the ground, try to square your HIPS to home plate — but keep your throwing shoulder back as long as possible. Feel the twist in your core? That's separation — that's where your velocity comes from! The longer you can keep your shoulder back before it fires, the more power you'll generate.

drills.drill_name: Stride Direction Drill — Using a Chalk Line or Tape
drills.description: A chalk line or tape strip is placed from the pitcher's rubber toward home plate. Pitchers work on landing their front foot just to the glove side of the line — stride direction that lines up their delivery toward the plate and prevents the common flaws of striding across or too far open.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: See this line? Your front foot should land just a little bit to the left of this line (for righties). Not crossing over it, not way off to the side — right next to it. Check where your foot lands after every throw. Landing on the line gives you the best chance to throw the ball straight to the plate.

drills.description: Isolate wrist snap for proper ball rotation.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Snap your wrist and pull your fingers down the back of the ball.

drills.description: The correct in-swing adjustment when a hitter recognizes off-speed mid-pitch — keeping the barrel in the zone instead of rolling over, for hitters facing pitchers who mix speeds.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Machine or feeder mixes speeds with a 2:1 fastball bias. Cue 'swing fastball, adjust down and long' — the barrel stays through the hitting zone so late recognition still produces fair contact. Track hard-hit rate on the off-speed only.
success_markers: Off-speed contact goes up the middle or oppo instead of weak pull-side
Posture holds through the adjusted swing
Hard-hit rate on off-speed climbs over 3-4 sessions

drills.drill_name: Glove-Side Pull Drill — Front Side Control
drills.description: Pitchers focus specifically on their glove arm — extending it toward the target during stride, then pulling it compactly into the ribs as the shoulder rotates. Proper glove-side control drives the chest toward the target and stabilizes the front side, increasing velocity and command.
common_flaws_fixed: glove arm flopping out to the side
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Point your glove toward home plate as you stride. Then as you throw, pull your elbow tight back into your ribs — don't let your glove arm flop out to the side like a wet noodle. When your glove goes IN, your chest goes FORWARD. That's what drives you toward the plate and makes you throw harder.

drills.drill_name: 9 Best Pitching Drills for Kids — Full Progression
drills.description: MOJO Sports presents 9 sequential pitching drills for kids including Flamingo (single-leg stability), Balance Beam (stride path with cones), Kneel of Fortune (upper body rotation), Towel Slap (arm extension), and more. A complete age-appropriate progression for coaches running youth pitching stations.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Work through each drill in order — they build on each other. Start with balance, then add the stride, then add the arm, then put it all together. Don't rush to throw full speed until each piece feels right. Great mechanics practiced slowly become great mechanics at full speed.

drills.description: After each pitch, the pitcher holds their finish position for 2-3 seconds. Checks for proper follow-through: back leg kicked up, chest over front knee, throwing hand by opposite hip, ready to field. Reinforces complete arm deceleration and finishing in an athletic fielding-ready position.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: After you throw, FREEZE in your finish position. Check yourself: Is your back leg up behind you? Is your chest over your front knee? Is your throwing hand down by your opposite hip? Are you ready to field a grounder? Hold it for 3 seconds. That's a complete, balanced finish.

drills.description: Rock back then drive hip toward home plate before arm begins.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Rock back, then drive your HIP first — not your shoulder!

drills.description: Lift knee to belt buckle and hold for 2-3 seconds.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Lift your knee and STOP. Hold for 2 seconds without wobbling.

drills.description: Use towel instead of ball to work on extension and release point.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Snap the towel on the target out in front!

drills.description: Kneel and throw using only forearm and wrist.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: From your knees, snap your wrist through the ball for backspin.

drills.description: Practice leg lift to balance point and hold.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Lift your knee to your belt and hold steady.

drills.description: Focus on leading with hip toward home plate.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Your hip goes first, your arm follows.

drills.description: Hold finish position after each pitch.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: FREEZE in your finish. Check your position for 3 seconds.

drills.drill_name: 10 Best Baseball Throwing Drills for Kids — Full Progression
drills.description: YouGotMOJO's definitive kids throwing drill video covers 10 sequential activities — from Extreme Catch (arm strength) to Bullseye (accuracy) to Over-Under (glove adaptability). Endorsed by WYAA and ideal for running as a full throwing station with ages 6-12.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Every good throw starts the same way: (1) Find the seams and grip the ball, (2) Step toward your target with your front foot, (3) Point your glove at the target, (4) Throw and finish with your arm across your body. Practice that pattern on every single throw — not just in drills, but in warm-up catch too.

drills.drill_name: Throwing Progression for Youth Players — Knee, Hip, Full
drills.description: Coach Duke and Coach Steve from Dominate the Diamond walk through the three-phase throwing progression: (1) kneeling throw to isolate arm action, (2) hip-width stance to add torso rotation, (3) full throw with stride. Endorsed by WYAA as a top youth throwing resource.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: We build your throw in three steps. First, from your knees — throw only using your arm and wrist snap. Second, stand wide and add a hip turn. Third, full throw with a step. Each step adds one more piece until you have the whole throw working together. Go slow first, then speed it up.

drills.description: Pro-level rundown execution at game speed — sprinting to close distance, ball visible above the shoulder, dart-throw timing, and rotating behind the play.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Use your fastest players as runners and score it: out in ≤2 throws = defense wins. Cue 'sprint, show, dart' — full-speed close, ball shown early, short dart throw on the receiver's call. Rotate at full speed.
success_markers: Defense wins 80% of reps vs. fast runners
Dart throws released on the receiver's call — never early
Rotation continues seamlessly through multiple throws when needed
drills.safety_notes: Game-speed dart throws at short range demand focus — receivers give a clear target away from the runner's head, and runners wear helmets.

drills.drill_name: First Base Fundamentals — Finding the Bag & the Stretch
drills.description: Core first-base play: getting to the bag, setting the feet, and basic stretch mechanics to receive throws. The starting point before picks and off-line throws.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue 'find it with your feet, face the thrower, stretch on release — not before.' Rep the footwork with no ball first: sprint to the bag from fielding depth, find it, set. Then add easy chest-high throws.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 8 reps (footwork only, then with throws)
success_markers: Finds the bag without looking down
Stretch happens as the throw is released, not as the fielder arrives
Heel contact maintained through the catch

drills.drill_name: Foul Line Throw — First Throw Introduction for Beginners
drills.description: A MOJO-recommended first-day throwing drill. Players line up on the foul line and throw into centerfield — no catching partner needed. Starts with wiffle balls for confidence, progresses to tennis then baseballs. Removes accuracy pressure and focuses purely on the step-and-throw motor pattern.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Today we just throw. Line up on the line, step toward center field, and let it go! Do not worry about where it goes — just step and throw. We start with wiffle balls so there is no pressure. The only goal: step TOWARD where you want the ball to go before you throw it.

drills.drill_name: Wall Ball Solo Drill — Partner-Free Mechanics Builder
drills.description: Dan Blewett's wall drill lets players practice full throwing mechanics solo. Throw against the wall, receive the rebound, and immediately throw again — building the catch-and-throw rhythm critical for all defensive positions. Perfect for home practice.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Do not just throw for fun — practice your mechanics on EVERY throw. Grip, step, throw, follow through. When the ball comes back, grip it quick and throw again. Work up to 50 throws in a row with perfect mechanics. Players who practice right at home improve much faster than those who only work at team practice.

drills.drill_name: Crow Hop — Arm Strength and Outfield Throwing
drills.description: Ultimate Baseball Training covers the crow hop — the skip-step used by outfielders to generate momentum before throwing. Correct footwork (hop, plant, stride, throw) multiplies power and distance. Essential for 8U+ players who play outfield and need to make longer throws.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: The crow hop is like winding up a throw with your whole body. After you catch the ball: hop onto your throwing-side foot, then stride forward with your front foot and throw. Hop, stride, throw! You will throw much harder when your whole body moves toward the target. Practice from short distance first, then go longer.

drills.drill_name: Extreme Catch — Progressive Distance Arm Builder
drills.description: Partners start close and take one step back each time both players catch cleanly. The pair that gets farthest wins. This game from YouGotMOJO builds arm strength naturally through progressive distance while keeping kids intensely engaged — the most game-like arm strength drill available.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Every time you both catch it, take one step back. The goal: get as far apart as possible before someone drops it! To throw far, use everything we practiced — crow hop, full arm swing, throw over your front foot. The farther you get, the more your whole body has to work. Who can make it the farthest?

drills.description: YouGotMOJO's Bullseye drill — players compete to hit a marked target at game-realistic distances. Points for hitting the bullseye create competitive pressure that simulates the focus needed to make accurate game throws.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Pick a spot on the target — the EXACT spot. Do not aim for the whole thing — aim for a spot the size of your fist. Before every throw, know exactly where you are throwing. Great throwers always have a precise target in mind. How many bullseyes in 10 throws? Challenge a teammate!

drills.drill_name: Over-Under — Two Ways to Throw and Catch
drills.description: Partners practice two throw types in sequence: a regular overhand throw caught fingers up, then a short underhand flip caught fingers down. Trains the glove position awareness and quick adaptability all infielders need.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Two throws, two catches. First: regular overhand — partner catches fingers UP. Second: underhand flip — partner catches fingers DOWN. Stay ready because it alternates! Baseball players have to catch balls at every height — this drill builds that awareness fast.

drills.drill_name: High Five Drill — Elbow Up Arm Path Correction
drills.description: Referenced across multiple youth coaching resources — the coach asks the player to give a high five with their throwing arm before each throw. This cue gets the elbow up to shoulder height in the correct pre-throw position, preventing the drop-arm sidearm habit that plagues young players.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Before you throw, give me a high five with your throwing hand! Elbow up, hand back — like you are about to high five someone behind your shoulder. THEN throw. That is the right arm position. If your elbow drops below your shoulder, your ball goes sideways instead of straight. Elbow up equals ball going straight!

drills.drill_name: Point-and-Go Glove Drill — Align Your Body to the Target
drills.description: Players point their glove elbow directly at their target before and during the throw. This simple point-and-go system automatically aligns the hips, shoulders, and chest toward the target, dramatically improving direction and accuracy for all age groups.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Point your glove at your target — like you are pointing with your finger — then throw. Your glove arm shows your body where to go! As you throw, your glove comes into your side and your chest turns to face where you pointed. Try it: point your glove at me, THEN throw. See how much straighter it goes? Point first, every single time.

drills.drill_name: Kneel-Down Throw — Isolating Upper Body and Wrist Snap
drills.description: Phase one of Dominate the Diamond's throwing progression. Both players kneel on their throwing-side knee, 15-20 feet apart. The arm, wrist, and torso must do all the work — isolating the exact upper-body mechanics needed for a strong, accurate throw. Perfect for correcting arm flaws without footwork distraction.
common_flaws_fixed: lower body interference with arm mechanics
drills.ai_coaching_notes: From your knees, throw using only your arm and wrist. Snap that wrist through the ball — like making it spin backward! Feel how your chest turns toward your partner as you throw? That is torso rotation adding power. Great arm mechanics first — then we add the legs.

drills.drill_name: Long Toss Progression — Building Arm Strength Safely
drills.description: Dan Blewett's safe long toss protocol for youth — start at 30 feet and build to maximum comfortable distance using the crow hop. Includes the crucial pulldown phase at the end to re-train accuracy after long toss. Safe, structured, and appropriate for 9-12 year olds when supervised.
equipment_needed: open field with 150+ feet of space
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Long toss builds arm strength — but only if done right. Start at 30 feet, throw easy. Move back only when your arm feels warm and throws feel good. At max distance, let the ball arc up — do not throw flat. Then do 5 to 10 throws pulling distance back in at the end. Never throw max effort in the first 10-15 throws.

drills.drill_name: Quick Hands Quick Feet — Fast Transfer Drill
drills.description: Pairs at short distance practice catching and transferring the ball to the throwing hand as fast as possible, then throwing back. Simulates the pressure of double-play footwork and quick-release infield throws. Referenced on Baseball Tutorials and multiple coaching resources.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: The ball comes out of your glove into your throwing hand as FAST as possible. Catch, transfer, throw. One motion, no pause. Your throwing hand should already be moving toward the ball as your glove closes on it. Time yourself: how fast can you catch it and throw it back? Compete with a partner.

drills.drill_name: Funnel Drill — Correct Arm Path Out of the Glove
drills.description: Dan Blewett's funneling concept — the ball should exit the glove going DOWN toward the hip, then arc UP as the arm swings through. This compact path separates accurate, safe throwers from kids who develop arm trouble and accuracy issues. Shown in slow-motion breakdown.
common_flaws_fixed: ball coming out going sideways or up
drills.ai_coaching_notes: When your hands separate, the ball comes out of your glove going DOWN toward your hip — not out to the side. From the hip, the ball goes UP and over as you throw. Think of an underhand swing that turns into an overhand throw. Watch slow motion: DOWN from glove, then UP through the throw. That is the funnel.

drills.drill_name: Clean Up Crew — Fun Fielding-to-Throw Game
drills.description: YouGotMOJO's Clean Up Crew game — balls are spread across the field and players throw them all into a designated bucket as fast as possible. Disguises throwing practice as a fun game, builds the pick-up-and-throw sequence, and keeps energy high.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Your job is to clean up all the balls and throw them into the bucket! For every ball you throw in, call out the count. Fastest player wins! But remember: a strong, accurate throw from your correct position gets the ball in. Rushing and throwing wild will not work. Use your mechanics even in a race!

drills.drill_name: Selfies Solo Rebounder — Build Reps Without a Partner
drills.description: YouGotMOJO's Selfies drill — throw at a wall or rebounder, catch the return, and throw again continuously. Builds the throw-catch-throw rhythm that is the foundation of all defensive play, letting players accumulate reps independently.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Throw, catch, throw, catch — keep a good rhythm going! Every time you catch it back, set your grip quickly and throw again with full mechanics. Count your reps. Can you get 25 in a row with good form? 50? Make good mechanics feel automatic so you do not have to think about them in a game.

drills.drill_name: Fun Fielding Drill for Young Players
drills.description: Former MLB infielder Matt Antonelli demonstrates an engaging fielding drill that young players love. Focuses on building confidence and proper mechanics in a fun, game-like format that keeps kids engaged while developing soft hands and proper glove positioning.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Keep your eyes on the ball. Get your glove out in front with fingers pointing down. Let the ball come to you — don't stab at it. Have fun and stay low like an alligator!

drills.drill_name: Throwing Accuracy Race — Competitive Catch Under Pressure
drills.description: Two pairs race to complete 10 accurate catches in a row — any bad throw or drop resets to zero. Forces players to maintain mechanics while feeling competitive pressure, simulating the mental challenge of making accurate game throws.
common_flaws_fixed: rushing and breaking down mechanics under pressure
drills.ai_coaching_notes: First pair to 10 catches in a row wins! Any bad throw or drop resets your count to zero. So make GOOD throws — not fast throws. Rushing and breaking your mechanics is how you reset the count. Slow is smooth, smooth is fast. Your best mechanics give you the best chance to win.

drills.description: Three-phase throwing progression: knee, hip, full throw.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Build your throw in three steps: knees, then hips, then full throw.

drills.description: Basic catching fundamentals - fingers up/down.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Fingers UP above belly, fingers DOWN below. Always two hands!

drills.description: Solo throwing practice against a wall.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Practice mechanics on EVERY throw. Grip, step, throw, follow through.

drills.description: Skip-step to generate momentum for outfield throws.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hop, stride, throw! Your whole body moves toward the target.

drills.description: Progressive distance throwing for arm strength.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start at 30 feet, build out slowly. Let the ball arc at max distance.

drills.description: Fast catch-to-throw transfer practice.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Catch, transfer, throw — one motion, no pause!

drills.description: Ball exits glove going DOWN, then UP through throw.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: DOWN from glove toward hip, then UP through the throw.

drills.description: Always catch with two hands for security.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Catch with glove, cover with throwing hand right away!

drills.description: Basic partner catch with proper mechanics.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Every throw: grip, step toward target, follow through.

drills.description: Pre-practice throwing warm-up routine.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start close, work back. Use full mechanics on every throw.

drills.description: Youth-specific work around the bag from a former pro: adjusting the feet to the throw and stretching to balls at different locations, with repeatable practice drills.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Throw intentionally to all four quadrants. Cue 'chase the ball with your glove-side foot' — the stretch foot moves toward the throw while the anchor toe holds the bag edge. Mix in throws from different infield angles.
drills.reps_guidance: 4 rounds of 6 throws (one round per quadrant)
success_markers: Stretch foot mirrors the throw location automatically
Anchor foot stays on the bag on wide throws
Clean catches on throws to both sides without crossing feet

drills.description: Coaches Duke Baxter and Steve Nikorak from Dominate the Diamond demonstrate 4 high-energy infield drills designed to keep youth teams engaged while building fundamental fielding skills with high-tempo reps.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Move your feet to the ball — don't wait for it to come to you. Field, transfer, throw — make it one smooth motion. Stay on the balls of your feet and stay ready. High energy, quick reps!

drills.drill_name: The Hands Routine — Infield Fielding Drill
drills.description: Former MLB first-round draft pick Matt Antonelli demonstrates his signature Hands Routine — the same pre-game routine he used as a professional. Teaches soft hands and clean glove-to-throwing-hand transfer through progressive solo drills that can be done anywhere.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Aim small, miss small — focus on exactly where the ball enters your glove. Soft hands — receive the ball, don't fight it. Practice the transfer: catch, grip, throw position. You can do this drill every day against a wall by yourself!

drills.drill_name: 3 Great Outfield Drills for Youth Players
drills.description: Coach Justin demonstrates 3 essential outfield drills for youth players covering drop step mechanics, proper fly ball tracking, and transitioning from catch to throw. Builds confidence in catching balls in the air.
common_flaws_fixed: backpedaling instead of turning and running
drills.ai_coaching_notes: First step is back — use your drop step, don't backpedal. Turn and run to where the ball will land, then adjust. Catch the ball above your throwing shoulder so you're ready to throw. Run on the balls of your feet to keep your eyes steady.

drills.description: Cal and Bill Ripken's instructional tip on the outfield drop step — the most fundamental outfield movement. Teaches youth players how to take a proper first step back on fly balls, turn the hips, and run efficient routes to the ball.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: When the ball goes over your head, don't run backward — drop step! Open your hips, turn, and RUN to the spot. Your first step is the most important step. Practice drop steps to both sides every day.

drills.drill_name: Essential Outfield Drills — Fly Balls and Ground Balls
drills.description: Coach Justin covers must-do outfield drills including fly ball tracking, proper catching position for quick transition to throwing, crow hop mechanics, and outfield ground ball technique with emphasis on game-like situations.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Catch the ball on your throwing side, not in the middle of your body. Use your crow hop — catch, step, hop, throw. On ground balls in the outfield, get around the ball and charge through it. Always know where you're throwing BEFORE the ball gets to you.

drills.drill_name: Stride Pause to Stride Swing Drill
drills.description: Players stride to a balanced landing position, PAUSE to feel the balance, then continue the swing. The pause eliminates rushing and teaches kids what being loaded and balanced feels like before triggering the swing.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stride forward with a small, soft step. Land and FREEZE — make sure you feel balanced before you swing. Your weight should be split evenly between both feet. Only after you feel balanced do you fire the swing. Take it slow until your body learns the feeling.
drills.reps_guidance: 2 sets of 8 — freeze 2 sec on the stride before swinging
success_markers: Lands in a balanced stride and can hold it still before swinging.

drills.description: A fundamental soft toss drill from Ripken Baseball where a partner kneels to the side and tosses balls into the hitter's strike zone. The hitter works on tracking the ball, timing the swing, and making solid contact at the proper point in front of home plate.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Watch the ball leave the tosser's hand. Let the ball get into your hitting zone before you swing. Stay balanced and drive through the ball toward the middle of the field.
success_markers: Lets the ball travel into the zone and squares it up on a line.

drills.description: A feeder throws underhand from behind a screen or L-screen directly in front of the hitter at a realistic ball path. Closer to game speed than soft toss, this drill bridges the gap between tee work and live pitching while keeping it safe and controlled.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Watch the ball from the moment it leaves the feeder's hand. Stay back — don't commit your weight until you see the ball. Make contact out in front. Your goal: line drives back through the middle. Keep your head down through contact.
success_markers: Drives line drives up the middle against game-speed tosses, on time.

drills.description: Hitters use only their top hand to swing at a ball on the tee. The top hand's job is to drive through the ball with the palm facing up at contact. This drill builds top-hand strength and teaches proper bat-path extension.
equipment_needed: one-hand training bat or short bat
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hold the bat with just your top hand. Drive through the ball like you're hitting it with your palm facing up — like you're serving a pizza! Finish with your hand high. If the ball goes weak to the pull side, your hand is rolling over too early.
drills.reps_guidance: 2 sets of 8 with a light bat
success_markers: Drives through the ball palm-up with a short, direct path.

drills.drill_name: The Swing Rail / Stay Inside the Ball Drill
drills.description: Using a Swing Rail or improvised PVC guide, players keep their front elbow connected to their body at the start of the swing. If the connection breaks, the loop in the swing is immediately visible — instant feedback teaching a compact, connected path to the ball.
equipment_needed: SwingRail training aid (or make with PVC)
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Keep your front elbow close to your body as you start your swing. If it flares out, that's casting — and you'll be late on every fastball. Think of keeping a piece of paper trapped between your elbow and your side until your hands get going. Then extend!
success_markers: Front elbow stays tucked — no flare-out at the start of the swing.

drills.description: Players stand approximately one bat-length from a fence and simulate swings on inside pitches. The fence gives immediate physical feedback — if the hands cast outward (casting), the bat hits the fence. Players learn to keep hands inside and drag the barrel through.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stand close to the fence — only about one bat-length away. Now imagine an inside pitch and swing. Your hands have to go INSIDE the ball or you'll hit the fence. Hands in, barrel through. If you hit the fence, your hands went outside the ball first. Try again!
success_markers: Swings without hitting the fence and drives the ball the other way.

drills.description: Players work on building a proper batting stance from the ground up — feet shoulder-width apart, knees bent, slight forward lean creating an axis to swing around. This is the foundation drill from YouGoProBaseball's 7-drill hitting progression.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stand like you're about to jump — knees bent, weight on the balls of your feet. Create a slight tilt with your upper body so you have an axis to rotate around. Hold the bat with your knocking knuckles lined up. Stay relaxed — not stiff!
success_markers: Sets up athletic and balanced every time without a reminder.

drills.drill_name: Mini Wiffle Ball & Skinny Bat Drill
drills.description: One of the hardest and most effective youth hitting drills. Players hit tiny wiffle balls with a narrow training bat, forcing extreme focus and precision. When they can make consistent contact with this setup, hitting a regular baseball feels effortless.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: This one is HARD — and that's the point! Keep your eyes on the tiny ball all the way until you make contact. Don't swing early. Trust your hands. When you can hit these consistently, real baseballs will look like beach balls. Practice until you can hit 7 out of 10.
success_markers: Tracks the tiny ball all the way to contact and makes consistent contact.

drills.drill_name: Tee Work — Ball Out In Front
drills.description: The tee is positioned out in front of home plate to force hitters to make contact at the ideal point — in front of the body. Coach Justin walks through proper tee setup and swing fundamentals from stance through follow-through.
common_flaws_fixed: hitting the ball too deep in the zone
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Set the tee just in front of your front foot. Hit the ball there. You should feel like you're reaching out to it — that's extension! Try to hit line drives right back at the middle of the net or field. The ball should come off the tee with a snap, not a thud.
success_markers: Makes contact out in front and drives line drives, not weak grounders.

drills.description: Teaches hitters to stay centered and balanced through the swing using back knee position.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue: athletic posture + keep hands above ball; match bat path to pitch plane.
success_markers: Stays centered over the back side without drifting forward.

drills.description: Hitting off a tee to work on swing fundamentals.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Set the tee out in front. Hit line drives to the middle.
success_markers: Hits firm line drives back up the middle, not pop-ups or choppers.

drills.description: Tee set low to practice low-pitch swings.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stay in your legs. Drive through the ball.
success_markers: Stays in the legs and drives low pitches on a line, not under them.

drills.drill_name: Line Drive Pro / Visual Feedback Swing Drill
drills.description: Using a Line Drive Pro trainer (or improvised equivalent), the ball provides immediate visual feedback on barrel angle — if the swing path is correct, the ball flies straight back; incorrect paths cause the ball to deflect in the wrong direction.
equipment_needed: Line Drive Pro trainer (or tennis ball on tee)
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Watch where the ball goes after you hit it. If it goes straight back — perfect swing! If it goes to the right, you cut across the ball. If it goes left, you rolled over it. Let the ball tell you what your swing is doing. Fix it one swing at a time.
success_markers: Ball flies straight back off the bat (level path) on most swings.

drills.description: Coach Duke Baxter (former pro player) walks through a systematic throwing progression covering proper 4-seam grip, arm action checkpoints, the high-five drill, throwing to targets, wall throws, shuffle steps, and quick hands — building mechanics incrementally from basic to game-speed.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Fingers on top of the ball. Show the ball to center field on your arm swing. Point your glove at the target. Step toward your target with every throw. Master each step before moving on.
drills.reps_guidance: 2 sets of 10 throws through the progression
success_markers: Shows a 4-seam grip, steps to the target, and follows through every throw.

drills.drill_name: How to Throw a Baseball — Complete Beginner Mechanics
drills.description: Dan Blewett's foundational throwing mechanics guide covers every step from grip to follow-through with slow-motion demonstrations. Critically debunks the scarecrow arm position commonly taught to young players and replaces it with the correct compact arm path.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Important: we do NOT do the scarecrow — arms out wide to the side before throwing. Instead: ball comes out of your glove going DOWN near your hip, then swings UP as your arm comes through. Elbow stays at shoulder height. Step toward your target. Throw and finish with your hand near your opposite hip.
success_markers: No "scarecrow" — the ball comes up out of the glove in a smooth arm circle.

drills.drill_name: How to Throw the RIGHT WAY
drills.description: Coach Lou Colon breaks down proper throwing mechanics to prevent arm pain and maximize velocity.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue: glove-side target; separate on time; smooth arm circle; good follow-through.
success_markers: Throws with a clean arm circle and finishes over the front side, no arm pain.
drills.safety_notes: Warm up first; keep throws age-appropriate; stop if pain.

drills.drill_name: The Ankle Eye Drill — Footwork Foundation
drills.description: Teaches the ankle eye concept from MOJO's Dan Keller — the inner ankle bump of the throwing-side foot should face the target after fielding. Step with the front foot toward the target and shoulders automatically align. A simple, memorable cue that immediately fixes the most common footwork flaw in youth players.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: After you catch the ball, look at the inside bump of your back foot — your ankle eye. Point it at your target. Then step toward your target with your front foot. Those two things automatically line up your shoulders for an accurate throw. Ankle eye, step, throw. Say it every time!
success_markers: Points the back-foot "ankle eye" and lands stepping right at the target.

drills.drill_name: 3 Simple Fielding Drills for Youth Players
drills.description: Coach Justin demonstrates 3 simple, beginner-friendly fielding drills for youth players focusing on proper fielding stance, getting low, and cleanly receiving ground balls with correct hand position.
common_flaws_fixed: not getting in front of the ball
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Get your butt down low. Watch the ball all the way into your glove. Use two hands — glove hand catches, throwing hand covers. Field the ball out in front of you, not between your feet.
success_markers: Fields with butt down, glove out front, and watches it into the glove.

drills.description: Official Little League video demonstrating a four-cone drill progression for fielding ground balls. Cones create a structured pathway that teaches players proper approach angles and footwork patterns when fielding.
common_flaws_fixed: not getting in front of the ball
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Use the cones as your guide — shuffle your feet to get in front of the ball. Stay low with your glove on the ground. Move through the ball, don't stop and wait for it. Your feet do most of the work!
success_markers: Shuffles to get in front of the ball and fields through it moving forward.

drills.drill_name: How to Get a T-Baller to Catch a Ball
drills.description: Coach Ballgame breaks down fundamental steps to teaching young athletes how to catch with confidence.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue: thumbs together above waist, pinkies together below; 'give' with hands.
success_markers: Keeps eyes on the ball and catches with two hands without flinching.

drills.drill_name: EASY Baseball Catch Drill — First Catch Fundamentals
drills.description: Bay Island Baseball's beginner catch drill breaks down the two most important catch fundamentals: fingers UP for balls above the waist, fingers DOWN for balls below. Also enforces two-hand catching at all times. Endorsed by WYAA as a go-to resource for new players.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Here is the glove rule: ball above your belly button — fingers UP. Ball below your belly button — fingers DOWN. And ALWAYS use two hands! Catch with your glove, then cover it with your throwing hand right away. Two hands protects the ball and gets you ready to throw faster.
success_markers: Uses "fingers up" above the waist, "fingers down" below — catches cleanly.

drills.drill_name: Balance Point Drill — Leg Lift & Pause
drills.description: Pitchers lift their front leg to their balance point (knee to belt buckle) and hold for 2-3 seconds. The pause isolates balance and forces pitchers to find a stable, repeatable balance position — the foundation of a consistent, accurate delivery. From MOJO Sports' 9 Best Pitching Drills for Kids.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Lift your knee up to your belt buckle and STOP. Hold for 2 seconds. Can you hold it without wobbling? Your front foot should hang straight down — not tucked behind your knee. Your eyes stay on the target the entire time. A pitcher who can't balance on one leg can't throw strikes consistently.
success_markers: Holds the leg lift balanced for 2 seconds without wobbling or falling forward.

drills.drill_name: 4-Part Windup Drill — Breaking Down the Delivery
drills.description: The complete pitching motion is broken into 4 distinct parts: (1) Starting position, (2) Balance point/leg lift, (3) Stride and arm separation, (4) Release and follow-through. Pitchers perform each part in slow motion, stopping to check each position before moving to the next.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Stop at each checkpoint: (1) Set position — are you balanced? (2) Balance point — knee up, foot loose? (3) Arm up, stride toward home? (4) Release out front and follow through? Master each stop before putting them together at full speed. Every great pitcher can do this slowly before doing it fast.
success_markers: Stops balanced at each checkpoint instead of rushing through the motion.

drills.drill_name: The Swing Shuffle Drill — Momentum & Rhythm
drills.description: The Swing Shuffle is a rhythm-based pitching drill where players build momentum through a lateral shuffle step before delivering. Creates fluid, athletic pitching mechanics and teaches pitchers how to transfer energy from the lower body up through the throwing arm — the same concept as a crow hop but applied to pitching.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Shuffle toward home plate to build momentum — then deliver the pitch. Feel the difference in how hard you can throw with momentum versus from a dead stop! Your lower body creates energy, your arm delivers it. A good pitcher's power starts in the ground and travels up through the whole body.
success_markers: Builds momentum smoothly and stays on time — not rushed or out of sync.

drills.drill_name: Advanced First Base — Off-Line Throws, Picks & Short Hops
drills.description: Academy-level footwork around the bag: shifting for throws to either side, timing the stretch, and picking short hops — the stretch goal for travel-level first basemen.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Feed short hops on purpose — start with announced hops, progress to random. Cue 'soft glove through the hop, not at it.' Add baserunner pressure last: a runner sprinting the line forces real stretch timing.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 sets of 8 picks (announced, random, with runner)
success_markers: Picks 6+ of 8 random short hops cleanly
Chooses stretch vs. leave-the-bag correctly on wild throws
Footwork holds up with a live runner
drills.safety_notes: Short-hop volume is hard on the glove hand — use tennis balls or soft baseballs for high-rep sessions.

drills.description: Five daily backhand drills training glove angle, footwork, and body position on balls to the glove-side and backhand side — the range and glove control travel-ball infielders need.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run as a daily 10-minute series from knees to full speed. Cue 'thumb down, see the ball into the glove, work through it.' The right foot plants outside the ball on a true backhand — check plant position every rep.
success_markers: Fields backhands with the glove out front — not beside the body
Plant foot consistently outside the ball
Converts backhand to throw without extra steps

drills.description: Five coach-friendly methods for teaching hitters to drive the ball the other way — the foundation for hitting behind runners and executing situational at-bats.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start on the tee set deep in the zone. Cue 'let it get to your back hip, hit the inside half.' Progress through the five methods as each sticks. Success is direction, not distance — a firm ground ball the other way counts.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 10 swings, all must go opposite field
success_markers: Ball flight consistently between center and the opposite-field line
Contact point is visibly deeper than the pull-side swing
Can call 'oppo' and execute on demand in BP

drills.description: Rapid-fire three-ball slow roller drill: charge, field on the run, and throw on the move under time pressure — the do-or-die play against fast runners.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Three balls spaced progressively closer — the fielder charges, fields, and throws each in sequence with no reset. Cue 'right foot, left foot, throw' rhythm on the run. Bare-hand only when the ball has stopped.
success_markers: Fields the ball outside the glove-side foot on the run
Throw releases within two steps of fielding
Accurate to first on all three balls of a circuit
