drills.safety_notes: Throwing on the run stresses the arm — full warm-up first and cap circuits for youth arms.

drills.description: Double-play footwork, feeds, and pivots at second base for both middle-infield positions — game-speed exchange and turn mechanics for 12-14U middle infielders.
common_flaws_fixed: slow transitions from catch to throw
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Rep feeds first (chest-high, at the bag), then turns without a runner, then with a soft slide. Cue 'give him the ball where his hands start.' Alternate 4-6-3 and 6-4-3 every round so both players learn both ends.
success_markers: Feeds arrive chest-high at the bag every rep
Pivot man's exchange takes one step or fewer
Full turn (contact to first-base catch) under a coach-set time target
drills.safety_notes: Teach bag footwork that clears the runner's path; no live hard slides in practice turns.

drills.drill_name: Call It Early — Outfield Communication Basics
drills.description: Introduces calling the ball — loud, early 'mine, mine, mine' between outfielders — with a simple drill format that builds the habit and prevents collisions.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Toss high flies between two fielders. Rule: the call must come before the ball's peak, three times loud. The other player answers 'take it, take it' and peels away. Start with soft balls so nobody fears the collision.
success_markers: Call comes before the ball peaks
Non-catching player audibly yields and peels off
Zero silent drops between fielders in scrimmages

drills.description: A practice-plan drill covering fly-ball priority between infielders and outfielders — who calls it, who peels off — plus ready-position habits, straight from the ABCA.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hit tweeners between the infield and outfield on purpose. Teach the rule plainly: the outfielder coming in owns any ball he can reach — infielders yield to his call. Freeze the play after each rep and ask 'whose ball, and why?'
success_markers: Outfielder's call overrides the infielder every time
Infielder peels off without stopping in the landing zone
Tweeners get caught instead of dropping between frozen fielders

drills.description: A team-wide competitive bunting game scoring sacrifice bunts, push bunts, and bunting for a hit — pressure and accountability so bunting practice transfers to games.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Split the team; each hitter draws a situation card (sac to third, push past the pitcher, squeeze). Points only for executed bunts against live pitching. Losing team does field cleanup — pressure makes the reps real.
success_markers: Executes 3 different bunt types against live pitching
Success rate climbs across sessions
Players choose the right bunt for the situation without coaching

drills.description: The outfield do-or-die play: charging a ground ball hard, fielding off the glove-side foot, and releasing quickly to cut down a runner at the plate.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Only for game-on-the-line situations — teach the distinction from the routine knee-down block. Cue 'attack, glove-side foot, crow hop through the ball.' Chart throw time and accuracy to a plate-sized target.
success_markers: Fielding happens off the glove-side foot at speed
Momentum continues through the throw toward the target
Throw is catchable at the plate on a line or one long hop
drills.safety_notes: Max-effort throws — warm up fully and cap at 8 reps per session for youth arms.

drills.drill_name: Oppo Tee & Toss — Stay Inside the Ball
drills.description: A repeatable tee/toss drill for staying inside the ball and driving outside pitches the other way — plugs directly into situational BP rounds.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Tee on the outer third, slightly deep. Cue 'knob to the ball, barrel late.' Rolling over the outside pitch means the barrel released early — reset with three one-arm bottom-hand swings, then return to full swings.
drills.reps_guidance: 4 sets of 8 swings on the outer-third tee
success_markers: Line drives to the opposite gap off the outer-third tee
No rolled-over contact for a full set
Same swing shows up on outside pitches in front toss

drills.description: Step-by-step introduction to holding and throwing a traditional changeup, built for youth hands: burying the ball deep in the palm and throwing with fastball intent.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start at short distance playing catch with the grip — no mound. Cue 'throw the fastball, the grip does the work.' If the ball sails, the grip is too shallow; if it dies into the dirt, too deep. Find the middle.
drills.reps_guidance: 15-20 changeup throws within a normal catch session
success_markers: Arm speed looks identical to the fastball from behind
Ball comes out 8-10% slower without being aimed
Comfortable enough to throw it in a bullpen without hesitation
drills.safety_notes: The changeup is the safe first off-speed pitch for youth arms — no curveball spin. Keep total throwing volume within normal daily limits.

drills.drill_name: Teaching the Changeup — Fastball Arm, Slower Ball
drills.description: A pro coach's method for developing the changeup with young pitchers: grip selection for small hands and keeping arm speed identical to the fastball so the pitch actually deceives.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Film from the side: the fastball and changeup deliveries should be indistinguishable. Common fault is slowing the arm — fix it by cueing 'throw it hard' and letting the grip kill velocity. Mix 1 changeup per 3 fastballs in bullpens.
drills.reps_guidance: 10-12 changeups per bullpen, mixed with fastballs
success_markers: Side-by-side video shows matching arm speed
Changeup lands in the bottom half of the zone
Hitters in live BP are visibly out in front
drills.safety_notes: Introduce off-speed only after fastball mechanics are stable; changeup before any breaking ball for youth pitchers.

drills.drill_name: Changeup Grip Menu — Match the Grip to the Hand
drills.description: Walks through circle, three-finger, and other changeup grip options so pitchers can match a grip to their hand size as they grow — and refine feel and movement.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Have the pitcher test 2-3 grips over two weeks of catch play and keep whichever kills the most speed with the least effort. Small hands usually can't do a true circle — three-finger is the honest starting point. Revisit each off-season as hands grow.
drills.reps_guidance: 10 throws per grip during catch play
drills.frequency_guidance: 2-3x/week for two weeks, then settle on one
success_markers: Picks one grip and can describe why it fits
Consistent 8-12% speed gap off the fastball
Some arm-side fade develops as pronation improves
drills.safety_notes: Grip experiments stay within normal catch-play volume; no max-effort mound work while testing grips.

drills.drill_name: The Catch Drill — Track & Read Pitches
drills.description: Hitters catch pitches instead of swinging, training the eyes to read pitch type and location out of the hand — recognition and discipline without swing pressure.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Hitter stands in the box wearing a helmet with a glove and catches the pitch, calling 'fastball' or 'change' as early as possible. Score correct early calls. Rotate hitters standing in during bullpens for free reps.
success_markers: Calls pitch type before the ball is halfway home
Correctly takes balls and 'catches strikes' by location call
Carries calmer takes into live at-bats
drills.safety_notes: Helmet required when standing in the box; start with reduced-speed pitching for younger hitters.

drills.description: What 'staying back' actually means, with drills to keep weight and hands loaded so hitters aren't fooled out front by off-speed pitches.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Front toss with random speed changes: the feeder varies fast/slow without telling. Cue 'stride to hit the fastball, keep the hands back for the change.' The stride lands on time — the hands wait.
success_markers: Head and weight stay behind the front hip on slow pitches
Hard contact on both speeds within the same round
No double-stride or lunge when fooled

drills.description: The 'move 'em' at-bat — advancing a runner from second with nobody out — broken down with College World Series examples: approach, pitch zones, and execution under pressure.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run situational BP: runner at second, nobody out, hitter must move him. Only pitches middle-away get swings — pulling a ball on the ground to short is a failed rep even if it's a 'hit.' Score execution, not outcomes.
drills.reps_guidance: 2 situational rounds of 6 at-bat scenarios per session
success_markers: Runner reaches third on 4+ of 6 execution reps
Hitter can state the plan before stepping in
Takes the inside pitch he can't execute with, without frustration

drills.description: Overload/underload training with weighted and light bats to raise bat speed in youth hitters — how to sequence heavy-light swings safely for developing players.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Order matters: heavy (feel sequence) → light (move fast) → game bat (transfer). Full intent on every swing — lazy overload swings teach slow. Measure with a swing sensor or simple phone video if no sensor.
success_markers: Game-bat swing speed measurably up over 4-6 weeks
Swing sequence stays intact under the heavy bat
No grip/wrist soreness — load is age-appropriate
drills.safety_notes: Keep overload bats within ~20% of game bat weight for youth; stop if wrist or elbow soreness appears.

drills.description: A simple high-rep bunting drill that trains deadening the ball and placing bunts toward first or third on command — precision beyond basic technique.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Lay towels or cone lanes down each line. Feeder calls 'first side' or 'third side' mid-toss. Cue 'catch it with the barrel' — soft top hand gives with contact. Chase the ball angle with the knob, not the barrel.
drills.reps_guidance: 3 rounds of 10 bunts, alternating target lanes
success_markers: 7+ of 10 bunts stop inside the called lane
Ball dies within 15 feet of the plate
Bat starts at the top of the zone — anything above it is taken

drills.description: Eight exercises pitchers should do after bullpens or game outings to flush the arm and protect the rotator cuff — a consistent recovery habit between outings.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: The routine happens within 15 minutes of the last pitch, every outing — consistency is the entire point. Keep everything light and rhythmic; recovery work should feel easier than warm-up work. Log soreness the next day to show players it works.
drills.reps_guidance: 1 round of 8 exercises immediately after throwing
drills.frequency_guidance: After every bullpen, start, or heavy throwing day
success_markers: Next-day soreness noticeably reduced in the player's log
Routine completed unprompted after outings
Full pain-free range of motion maintained through the season
drills.safety_notes: Recovery work is light by design — no heavy resistance after throwing. Persistent sharp pain after outings is a see-a-doctor sign, not a push-through sign.

drills.drill_name: Youth Receiving Foundations — Quiet Glove & Soft Hands
drills.description: First receiving progression for young catchers: glove presentation, soft hands, and catching the ball with slight momentum toward the strike zone. Fixes stabbing and hard hands behind the plate.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Start bare-glove with tennis balls from short distance. Cue 'catch the ball moving toward the zone, not away.' Watch for the elbow locking out — a slightly bent elbow keeps hands soft.
success_markers: Glove is quiet after the catch instead of drifting
Catches low pitches without turning the glove over
Ball stops moving toward the zone edge, not out of it
drills.safety_notes: Use tennis balls or soft training balls for bare-hand/receiving-only work; full gear whenever catching live throws.

drills.description: Five MLB-style receiving drills scalable to any age: beating the ball to the spot, sticking pitches, and working the edges of the zone. The middle step once basic soft hands are in place.
mechanic_focus: beat the ball to the spot
common_flaws_fixed: carrying pitches out of the zone
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run as a 5-station circuit. Cue 'beat it to the spot' — glove arrives where the pitch will be before the ball does. Freeze each catch for a one-count to build the stick habit.
success_markers: Borderline pitches are caught and held in the zone
Glove beats the ball to the spot on edges
Umpire-view video shows the ball 'stuck' rather than dragged

drills.description: YouGoProBaseball presents three progressive framing drills teaching catchers to receive pitches with quiet, soft hands while subtly presenting borderline pitches as strikes. Covers proper wrist positioning for inside, outside, high, and low pitches.
common_flaws_fixed: pulling pitches out of the zone
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Catch the ball and STICK it — don't move your glove after catching. On outside pitches, thumb goes down. On inside pitches, turn your mitt slightly in. Make every pitch LOOK like a strike. Start barehand with a rolled-up sock to learn the feel.
success_markers: Catches and sticks the pitch quietly with no glove drift, stealing the edges of the zone.

drills.description: Team drill teaching proper communication on fly balls between outfielders.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Cue: first step back; get under ball; use two hands; call it early.
drills.reps_guidance: 2 sets of 8 fly balls between two outfielders
success_markers: One player calls it early and loud, the other peels off - no collisions, nothing drops between them.
drills.safety_notes: Clear communication; watch for collisions.

drills.description: Modern one-knee-down receiving: five drills to master framing from the stance MLB catchers use, at higher pitch speeds. For experienced catchers ready for the progression ceiling.
common_flaws_fixed: carrying pitches out of the zone
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Only introduce after two-knee receiving is consistent. Check the free leg still allows a block or throw. Increase pitch speed gradually — machine work is ideal for high-rep edges.
drills.reps_guidance: 4 sets of 10 receives per setup (RH low, LH low, edges)
success_markers: Low strike is presented without dropping the glove head
Can still block and throw from one knee
Holds the bottom-zone strike at game velocity

drills.description: Essential J-band resistance exercises for youth pitchers and throwers: warming up the shoulder and building arm strength before any throwing session.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Anchor at elbow height and keep tension light — these are activation reps, not strength maxes. Cue 'slow out, slow back' with no band snap. Make it the non-negotiable first station before any throwing.
drills.reps_guidance: 1 round of 8-10 reps per exercise, before every throwing session
success_markers: Completes the routine without form breakdown
Reports the arm feeling 'ready' before the first throw
Routine happens without being reminded
drills.safety_notes: Light resistance only for youth — bands should bend, not strain. Stop any exercise that causes joint pain rather than muscle warmth.

drills.description: A nine-exercise J-band routine targeting the rotator cuff and scapular muscles for throwing durability and velocity — proper band tension, tempo, and the common form mistakes.
drills.ai_coaching_notes: Run as a standalone mini-workout on lighter throwing days, not tacked onto a max-effort session. Cue controlled 2-second tempo each direction. Elbows stay at the set height — dropping the elbow is the giveaway fatigue sign to stop.
success_markers: All 9 exercises completed with steady tempo
Band resistance can progress after 3-4 weeks
Arm bounces back faster between outings
drills.safety_notes: Strength band work belongs on low-throwing days; skip it the day after a max pitch-count outing.

problems.description: Pops bunts up, misses entirely, or can't place them — no reliable sacrifice bunt.

problems.description: Arm gets tired or sore across the season; no band work or recovery routine to build durability.
